message.content: {"key_mechanism_gt": "Specific pyranopyrazole derivatives (4c for antibacterial and 4e for antifungal) exhibit potent activity by forming stable, long-lasting complexes with dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) enzymes, with 4c binding preferentially to bacterial DHFRs (e.g., from Staphylococcus aureus) and 4e binding preferentially to Candida albicans DHFR, as evidenced by favorable binding energies and low Cα RMSD values during 250 ns MD simulations.", "key_mechanism_gen": "The N-substituent on the pyranopyrazole scaffold sterically and electronically pre-organizes the heterocycle to form a dual H-bond network with Arg212 and Glu157 of the S. aureus ATP synthase c-subunit, blocking ADP/ATP exchange while minimizing off-target binding to human ATP synthase.", "recovery": "NOT_RECOVERED", "rationale": "The generated hypothesis proposes inhibition of ATP synthase via H-bonding with Arg212 and Glu157, while the ground truth reveals inhibition of DHFR via stable complex formation, representing entirely different molecular targets and mechanisms."}
